posting.title: Senior Frontend Engineer, Design Systems
posting.rawText:
Senior Frontend Engineer, Design Systems
Northwind Commerce · Remote (India or EU time zones) · Full time

Northwind Commerce builds checkout and storefront software for mid-sized retailers. Our design system is used by four product teams and ships every week.

What you will do
- Own the Northwind design system: components, tokens and the Storybook documentation.
- Raise the bar on accessibility and performance across the checkout.
- Partner with designers on Figma-to-code handoffs and review pull requests for the web team.

Requirements
- Must have 5+ years building production web applications with React and TypeScript.
- Deep experience owning a component library or design system used by several teams.
- Practical accessibility experience: WCAG 2.1 AA audits and fixes.
- Experience with automated testing: unit tests with Vitest or Jest and end-to-end tests with Playwright.
- Strong command of web performance: Core Web Vitals, LCP and bundle budgets.
- Experience with GraphQL APIs, ideally Apollo Federation.

Preferred
- Experience mentoring engineers and leading code review.
- Experience with Next.js and React server components.

Nice to have
- Rust or WebAssembly experience.
- Open-source maintenance.

Eligibility
- Must be legally able to work in India or the EU without visa sponsorship from us.

Apply at https://jobs.northwind-commerce.example/frontend-design-systems

paragraphs.text: I am a Frontend Engineer II at Kitebird, where I own Kite UI, the shared React component library with 42 components, typed tokens and Storybook docs, used by 3 product squads. I also keep the public Storybook for the library. The Northwind design system role is about owning a library that several teams rely on, and that is the job I do today. I enjoy the unglamorous parts of it most: naming, documentation and keeping a change small enough to review. It is shared work, so I write for the people who will use the library as much as for the people who review it.

On accessibility, I ran a WCAG 2.1 AA audit of checkout with design and fixed the critical issues: focus order, labels, colour contrast and screen-reader announcements for cart updates. Your posting asks for practical accessibility experience, and this audit is that work from start to finish. I would bring the same approach to the checkout at Northwind Commerce: audit with the designers, fix the worst problems first and then keep the fixes from regressing.

On performance, I rebuilt the three-step checkout as a single-page flow in React and TypeScript with optimistic cart updates. Checkout conversion rose 9.4% in the A/B test and LCP on the payment step dropped from 4.1s to 1.9s. Earlier, at Saffron Ledger, I fixed table rendering performance for accounts with 10,000+ invoices using virtualised lists. In both places I started from a measurement and ended with one.
Thank you for your time. I would welcome a conversation about the role.
